problem: Roth's theorem in [N]: how large can a 3AP-free subset of {1,...,N} be?
board: Density increment with Bohr sets -- the board Kelley-Meka 2023 ran on, and the board Bloom-Sisask re-present with classical Bohr set machinery.

ceiling.quantity: the exponent e in |A| <= exp(-c (log N)^e) N; larger e is a stronger upper bound
ceiling.cap_scope: ANY argument that uses any sort of density-increment argument with Bohr sets, whether using Kelley-Meka ideas or a more traditional Fourier analytic approach -- the authors' own words, so the cap is on the BOARD, not on their argument

truth.what_establishes_it: Behrend 1946 constructs 3AP-free subsets of [N] of size at least exp(-c (log N)^{1/2}) N, with small improvements by Elkin 2011 and Green-Wolf 2010. So no upper bound with exponent above 1/2 can exist, and the truth is at exponent 1/2 or below it.

quote: Of course, the Behrend exponent of 1/2 would be the final target, but this seems quite far out of reach still; indeed, an exponent of 1/3 (or perhaps even 1/4) seems to be the limit of any argument that uses any sort of 'density increment' argument with Bohr sets (whether using Kelley-Meka ideas or a more traditional Fourier analytic approach).
source: arXiv:2302.07211v3 (Bloom, Sisask, 'The Kelley-Meka bounds for sets free of three-term arithmetic progressions'), 'Improvements' paragraph
source_as_of: 2025-05-13 (v3); the same paragraph also announces 1/9 and 5/41 as improvements on Theorem 1's 1/12

state_of_the_board_when_registered.announced_by_the_same_paper: 1/9 with a clean modification, 5/41 after technical optimisation
state_of_the_board_when_registered.so_the_gap_to_the_cap: even the believed natural limit 1/7 = 0.1429 is well short of the stated board cap 1/3 = 0.3333, which is itself short of the truth at 1/2

resolution_criterion: RESOLVES AS broken-on-the-same-board if an upper bound with exponent strictly above 1/3 is proved by a density-increment-with-Bohr-sets argument. RESOLVES AS held-and-board-left if an exponent above 1/3 is proved by an argument that is not of that kind, or if the authors' cap is superseded by a stated cap from the same board. Improvements at or below 1/3 that stay on the board (1/9, 5/41, 1/7, anything up to 1/3) resolve NOTHING: they are the cap being approached, which is what the statement predicts.

prediction.claim: The exponent will not pass 1/3 by a density-increment-with-Bohr-sets argument. If it passes 1/3 at all, it will be by leaving that board.
prediction.by: this session, sealed before any resolution exists
prediction.confidence: this is the AUTHORS' prediction, adopted rather than formed independently -- it is registered to test the REGISTER, not to display judgement of mine
prediction.horizon: unknown and probably long. Stated plainly: an item that may not resolve for a decade cannot validate a benchmark on this project's timescale. The register's value is that the label is not hindsight, not that it is fast.
